The count is DERIVED (evalir_coverage.derive_denominator over EMITTED_INSTS and the IRInst inductive), never typed here. Every syntax field of every IRInst constructor is classified; the erased align slots and the measured W1-W4, float-residue and Phase-B executor divergences have their permanent rows here.

rows.clean: ir_copy_eval checks the operand's SHAPE class against the declared type (bool / integer / float / thin pointer / fat pointer / unit / aggregate / function pointer / never) and faults type_error across classes — kernel witness ir_copy_ty_slot_is_read — but ACCEPTS within a class: two integer widths, the two signednesses, two aggregate ids, and the WHOLE thin-pointer family are indistinguishable to it. The enumeration is exhaustive as written: tuple/array/struct/enum share the aggregate class, and ptr_/ref_/refmut_/rawconst_/rawmut_/rc_ share the thin-pointer class WITH nullptr_, so `ir_copy_eval (IRTy.ref_ p) IRScalar.nullptr_` accepts where expect_ty faults
rows.e2: the reference's Inst::Copy arm calls expect_ty(operand, ty), a dynamic type EQUALITY on the value's own carried Ty, and faults type_error on any disagreement — width and aggregate id included
rows.measured: 2026-09-10 at trust 0dd9d3e2d7, against `Inst::Copy` (interpret.rs:691-696 — `expect_ty(operand, ty)?` then a rebind of the same value) and `fn expect_ty` (interpret.rs:5548-5557 — `if &value.ty == ty { Ok(()) } else { type_error }`). The residual is TWO-WAY and both directions are declared here. ACCEPT-MORE: a width, signedness or aggregate-id disagreement passes the shape check and would fail expect_ty. REJECT-MORE, fail-closed: the Copy arm never calls reject_partial (interpret.rs:6506-6515; its message at interpret.rs:6500-6501 states that poison may only be copied or stored, never inspected), so the reference transports poison VERBATIM where ir_copy_eval faults type_error at ir_scalar_shape's class 0 — unreachable on the executed fragment, because the model's only producer of a bound undef_ is IRInst.undef, itself the declared delta `undef-execution`. This row exists rather than an irrelevance theorem for copy.t because copy.t is READ: IRScalar carries no type tag (an int_ does not say its width, an aggv does not say its id), which is the same design choice that lets a cell hold a value instead of a byte image, so expect_ty is not statable in this model and the finest decidable partition is the shape class. The chain's own three copies (`copy ptr`, `copy ptr`, `copy struct.0`) are all cross-class-correct, so neither direction bears on them
rows.recorded_in: this grid row is the permanent home; the reference arm and the model arm are read side by side in eval_ir_machine.rs's COPY comment block

rows.clean: the encoding-aware load view decodes a matched aggregate type only when the cell holds a WORD-shaped scalar (ptr_ / nullptr_ / int_); at the same type an inline aggregate value passes through unchanged — kernel witness ir_view_agg_is_identity
rows.e2: the reference always decodes the BYTE IMAGE the store wrote, at the load's type, whatever produced it
rows.measured: 2026-09-10 at trust 0dd9d3e2d7, against decode_value's Niche arm (interpret.rs:3766-3796) and the store-side niche check (interpret.rs:3538-3567). NEITHER SIDE FAULTS in this row: it is a VALUE divergence, not a fault-direction one. The two agree exactly when the model's store/load round-trip and the reference's encode/decode round-trip are both the identity on a valid value, which is the case on this chain: `as_deref` writes an aggregate into its own alloca and reads it back (sidecar text: `store enum.0 %5, ptr %1` then `%14 = load enum.0, ptr %1`), while `%2 = load enum.1, ptr %0` reads a real heap word at the SAME kind of type. The decision is SHAPE-directed inside a type-directed dispatch, and the identity arm is not an accident — it is what keeps the chain alive on both the None and the Some path, and what makes the whole extension conservative on the eighteen chains that predate it. The carrier-constructor half of the row is the same class read the other way: the reference turns any 8-byte word at a pointer-payload type into a pointer VALUE KIND through resolve_pointer_kind, so an integer carrier becomes NullPtr / Ptr / DanglingPtr there and stays an int_ here
rows.recorded_in: this grid row is the permanent home; the shape-tolerance rule is stated in ir_niche_image's doc and pinned by ir_view_agg_is_identity

rows.clean: the machine's null is the scalar IRScalar.nullptr_; `ptr_ Nat.zero` is an ORDINARY address in its own address space, so a live cell at address 0 is loaded, stored and borrowed like any other — kernel witness ir_borrow_no_provenance_is_ub covers the missing-cell case, not this one
rows.e2: the reference's resolve_pointer_kind maps address 0 to NullPtr before it looks for an allocation, so every dereference of it — Load, Store and Borrow alike — is UB 'null pointer dereference'
rows.measured: 2026-09-10 at trust 0dd9d3e2d7, against `fn resolve_pointer_kind` (interpret.rs:5415-5423 — `if address == 0 { NullPtr } else if let Some(ptr) = self.try_pointer_from_address(address) { Ptr } else { DanglingPtr }`) and `fn expect_pointer` (interpret.rs:5648-5670). The direction is ACCEPT-MORE: the model continues where the reference is UB. This is the machine's PRE-EXISTING address-space convention, shared verbatim by ir_load_at and ir_store_at since the memory stage was written; it is recorded under `borrow` because Phase B is where it was measured, and it is reachable rather than theoretical — ir_alloca_k allocates at the machine's allocation counter, and every return-slot lemma is stated at an ABSTRACT counter, which includes zero. A zero test in the arms would close it and would also make each of them stuck at that abstract counter, so it is declared rather than taken
rows.recorded_in: this grid row is the permanent home; the reasoning is in eval_ir_machine.rs's BORROW comment block, which is also where the load/store sharing is stated

rows.clean: ir_borrow_slot resolves the address through ir_mem_lookup and faults `ub bad_addr` when no LIVE cell answers; ir_alloc_cells materialises cells only at base .. base+k-1, so a one-past-the-end address has no cell and the borrow faults — kernel witness ir_borrow_no_provenance_is_ub, which is exactly this no-cell minor read at an empty memory
rows.e2: the reference's try_pointer_from_address has a SECOND loop that accepts `address == allocation.base + allocation.size`, so a one-past-the-end address resolves to Ptr rather than DanglingPtr and expect_pointer admits the borrow
rows.measured: 2026-09-10 at trust 0dd9d3e2d7, against the second loop of `fn try_pointer_from_address` (interpret.rs:5396-5406) reached through `fn resolve_pointer_kind` (interpret.rs:5415-5423) and `fn expect_pointer` (interpret.rs:5648-5670). The direction is REJECT-MORE and therefore FAIL-CLOSED: the model refuses a borrow the reference performs, which can leave a chain stuck but cannot admit a false theorem. It is REACHABLE rather than theoretical — ir_gep_eval (the ir_gep_base off the ir_sum_idx sum) adds an unbounded offset with no bound check, so `ptr_ (base+k)` is constructible in the model exactly as it is in the reference — and it is SHARED verbatim with ir_load_at and ir_store_at, which resolve through the same ir_mem_lookup; it is recorded under `borrow` because Phase B's borrow arm is where it was measured. Closing it would mean giving the model an allocation table with bases and sizes rather than a flat cell list, which is a memory-model change and not a borrow-arm change, so it is declared rather than taken. The executed fragment does not exhibit it: the sidecar chain's geps are in-bounds field projections
rows.recorded_in: this grid row is the permanent home; the two-way residue is stated in eval_ir_machine.rs's BORROW comment block beside the address-zero one

rows.clean: a wide value is IRScalar.fat_ d md -- an ADDRESS and a WORD, with no null lane -- so ptr_from_parts over a null data pointer is `ub null_deref` (ir_ptrparts_eval) and over a null metadata pointer `type_error not_int` (ir_ptrparts_at)
rows.e2: eval_ptr_from_parts builds FatPtr { NullPtr, .. } -- validate_fat_pointer_value admits a Ptr, NullPtr or DanglingPtr data lane -- and, at a vtable kind, FatPtr { .., NullPtr }; the null fat pointer CONSTANT `{ 0, 0 }` is its const_value arm
rows.measured: 2026-09-27 at trust-ir dcc5b9a3, read off eval_ptr_from_parts, validate_fat_pointer_value and const_value's null fat pointer arm. REJECT-MORE, FAIL-CLOSED: the model halts where the reference builds a value, which can leave a chain stuck but cannot admit a false theorem. The projector refuses a CONSTANT at container_len, container_vtable and dyn.N by name (the null pair is the only one the reference admits there), and none of the four E5 slices of real m0off bodies carries a null lane
rows.recorded_in: this grid row is the permanent home; the design is decision memo §23, and the projector's refusal is its `Inst::Const` arm

rows.clean: the fat arm reads its word at the DECLARED metadata type alone (ir_ptrmeta_lane: a length at uint_ w, a vtable address at ptr_) and does not check that type against the POINTER type's canonical kind -- `pt` stays dropped (ir_exec_ptrmeta_pt_irrelevant) -- so a vtable word read at uint_ w binds an integer
rows.e2: eval_ptr_metadata refuses a declared metadata type that is not FatPtrKind::metadata_ty of the pointer type (type_error), a length for Slice/Str/ContainerLen and a thin Ptr for TraitObject/ContainerVtable
rows.measured: 2026-09-27 at trust-ir dcc5b9a3, read off eval_ptr_metadata. ACCEPT-MORE, on ILL-TYPED input only: trust-ir's validator refuses the pair statically (PointerMetadataTypeMismatch), and the projector refuses it by name (check_metadata_ty), so no validated module and no projected module carries one; on a canonical pair the two answer alike, which the E5 slices measure (ir_e5_ptrmeta_mt_is_read, ir_e5_ptrmeta_len_word)
rows.recorded_in: this grid row is the permanent home; ir_ptrmeta_lane's comment block in eval_ir_machine.rs states the arm

rows.clean: ir_icmp_eq / ir_icmp_ne ANSWER on pointer-shaped operands (ir_eqb over the comparable ptr_ / nullptr_ / fnptr_ constructors); on a WIDE pointer they halt type_error not_int (ir_e5_icmp_eq_containerlen_refused and its five siblings), which is exact
rows.e2: eval_icmp refuses EVERY non-integer operand, thin pointer or wide: expect_int_value raises type_error ('expected integer value, got ptr'); trust-ir's Lean semantics (semICmpInst, 'ICmp: non-integer operands') refuses the same
rows.measured: 2026-09-27 at trust-ir dcc5b9a3, by RUNNING the reference interpreter on tests/fixtures/e5/e5_m0off_slices.trust-ir.txt: e5::drive_control_thin_icmp (`icmp eq ptr %0, %0`) and e5::drive_ptr_eq (the `Arc::ptr_eq` fast path of <Name as PartialEq>::eq, `icmp eq fatptr<container_len>`) both end TypeError. ACCEPT-MORE on the THIN half: the model answers where the reference refuses, and the m0off callee sidecar carries 185 `icmp eq ptr` sites, so this is reachable, not theoretical. It is PRE-EXISTING (E5 found it, did not make it) and the wide half agrees. Closing it is a reference question -- the compiled program does compare pointers -- not a model one, so it is declared rather than taken
rows.recorded_in: this grid row is the permanent home; the measurement is tests/eval_ir/e5_fat_images.rs's E2 leg and decision memo §23

provenance.rule: field surface = IRInst telescopes (eval_ir_syntax.rs); read/drop verdict = word-boundary use of the arm's pattern variable in the ir_exec arm RHS (eval_ir_machine.rs); dropped fields must name a registered theorem; erased and delta rows must anchor to live source. Fail-closed on any mismatch. Gate: tests/eval_ir/adequacy_grid.rs re-derives the surface independently.
